audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven chart rows contradicted their own why strings: level 1 was K'Sante at 7/10 while the why concedes the level, levels 3 and 4-5 were Yone while the whys call them 'my full Q-W combo lands' and 'my tank control peak', and level 6 was K'Sante while the why calls it a coin-flip.
audit.why: Packet chart reads Skill / Skill / K'Sante / K'Sante / Skill / Skill / Yone, consistent with the 50.75% win rate over 1807 games. K'Sante owns 3 through 5, where Yone has no crit items; Yone owns the two-item window.
audit.corrected: All seven rows set to the packet chart with ratings inverted. Level 1's why also reworded — both Qs are 450-range lines with no engage, so it is genuinely a standoff, not a concede.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and Yone's abilities were never named — the packet flags exactly this.
audit.why: Soul Unbound is 22/19/16/13/10s — a 22-second rank-1 window is the biggest punish in lane and shrinks to 10s maxed. Spirit Cleave is 14s and shields. Mortal Steel is 4s with the 2-stack dash-knockup. Fate Sealed is 120/100/80s.
audit.corrected: Spikes and whys now name Mortal Steel, Spirit Cleave, Soul Unbound and Fate Sealed with real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The text says three times to 'W-charge the unstoppable wall-stun so his cleave can't break it'. K'Sante's W is not unstoppable in the data. Spirit Cleave's shield — the flagged missing interaction — was described only as damage, never as the thing that eats your opener. The Ntofo shockwave was called a knock-up.
audit.why: Riot's W text for K'Sante: 'charges up, taking reduced damage' — nothing about unstoppable. Riot's Spirit Cleave text: 'Grants a shield to Yone, the value is increased by the number of champions hit'. Riot's K'Sante Q text: the 2-stack shockwave 'pulls enemies in'.
audit.corrected: W is damage reduction into a stun; Spirit Cleave's 14s shield is now the thing you force out before committing; the shockwave pulls.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire content layer was written in the first person.
audit.why: The site speaks to the player in second person; this page reads as someone else's diary.
audit.corrected: whys, spikes, early, mid and late rewritten in second person at the same length.

edits.before: Level 1 I have only Q and no engage, so I concede the level and just farm at Ntofo Strikes range — Yone's Q dash and W spirit-cleave out-trade me if I step up early. Once I hit Level 2 for W or E I'm safer, and at Level 3 my full kit is online: this is my first real window. The key is to bait his Q dash — when he commits it I W-charge the unstoppable wall-stun so his cleave can't interrupt me, then Q3 knocks him up and pulls him in. Never throw a raw Q at a Yone holding his E; he'll spirit-rewind straight out of the pull.
edits.after: Level 1 you have only Q and no engage, so farm at Ntofo Strikes range — Mortal Steel matches it and Spirit Cleave beats you if you step up early. Level 2 makes you safer, and at Level 3 the full kit is online: your first real window. Bait the 2-stack Mortal Steel dash — when he commits it, W-charge him into a wall for the stun, then pull him in. Force Spirit Cleave out first; it shields him on 14s and eats your opener. Never throw a raw Q at a Yone holding Soul Unbound; he rewinds out of the pull.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are my lane-control peak as a tank — I trade around his Q-W cooldowns, eat his spirit-cleave on my armor, and bank small leads with my bulk while he has to walk into my Q range to farm. At 6 it goes even: All Out gives me a duelist profile that can win the straight 1v1, but it strips my tankiness, and his E spirit-rewind lets him undo my whole engage and reset the fight on his terms. So I don't pop R to greedily all-in a full-health Yone — I bait his E and W first, then commit when he has nothing to rewind to.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your lane-control peak as a tank — trade around Mortal Steel's 4s and Spirit Cleave's 14s, eat the cleave on your armour, and bank small leads while he must walk into Q range to farm. At 6 it goes even: All Out gives you a duelist profile that wins the straight 1v1, but it strips your bulk, and Soul Unbound — 22s at rank 1, 10s maxed — snaps him back to his body and repeats his damage. So never burn R on a full-health Yone: bait E and W first, then commit when he has nothing left to rewind to.

edits.before: This is where Yone reclaims it. With two crit or lethality items his Q3 knock-up into R does real burst, and his E rewind plus W cleave out-DPS my All-Out body once my tank stats are converted away — my armor stacking means nothing against a fed mobile carry. I can't bet on the very late 1v1, so I close on my Levels 3-5 and first-item windows where Iceborn Gauntlet and my W stun force fights he can't kite. Past two items I stop dueling him in the side lane and play for teamfights: survive his burst with W, then R All Out to yank him off my carry and drag him into my team.
edits.after: This is where Yone reclaims it. With two crit or lethality items the 2-stack Mortal Steel knockup into Fate Sealed is real burst, and Soul Unbound plus a stacked Spirit Cleave shield out-DPS your All Out body once your tank stats are converted away — armour stacking means nothing against a fed mobile carry. Don't bet on the very late 1v1: close on your Levels 3-5 and first-item windows, where Iceborn and the W stun force fights he cannot kite. Past two items, stop duelling in the side lane and play for fights — survive the burst, then R to launch him off your carry.
